the development of a vaccine for foot and mouth disease (FMD).
the development of vaccines for FMD and the use of pigs as models for the development of vaccines and for the study of transmission and pathogenesis of FMD virus.
the efficacy of high potency FMD vaccines in the protection of pigs against heterologous challenges.

a high potency (>5.5 log10 PD50) FMD vaccine can provide early protection in pigs and that transmission of virus within rooms can be prevented by vaccination.

the high potency O1Manisa monovalent FMD vaccine is efficacious against a heterologous challenge in pigs and provides early protection.

high potency vaccines provide protection against challenge in the absence of detectable antibodies and that transmission of FMDV within rooms is a very rare event.
